answer: A sybil-resistant registry can require each identity to post a refundable bond and pass a hardware attestation check, so one account is cheap but thousands are expensive. The bond is slashed if the same device or credential signs for two identities, making a mirror copy of an existing agent unprofitable rather than free. Newcomers join only through a small grove of trusted sponsors, each risking part of its own bond per invitee, so an attacker cannot plant an island of fake accounts without sponsors staking real value that proven fakes forfeit.
